answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly: each new agent needs an established peer to stake collateral vouching for it, and if the newcomer misbehaves the voucher gets slashed. So a sable-cloaked attacker spinning up a violet swarm of throwaway identities must find, and risk, real bonded capital for every single one. The honest attestation graph then reads an unvouched flood as noise, not signal, and the attacker cost scales linearly with each fake identity minted.
